title: College Application Manager - North Creek High School
content:
College Application Manager
The College Application Manager is a tool used by students to:
request application documents, such as transcripts and letters of recommendation,
manage & track application requirements,
add application results, and
indicate enrollment decisions
The College Application Manager is not where students submit their college applications. Applications are submitted directly on college websites or through applications portals such as Common App, Coalition, Questbridge, etc...
IMPORTANT NOTE: SchooLinks has a partnership with Common App !    This partnership simplifies the process of requesting and tracking application documents onto a single dashboard for students. if you are signed into your SchooLinks account, you can learn more:  How to Connect your Common App Account .  This website is an external link.  This website is not controlled or operated by the Northshore School District.
Set up College Application Manager
The first time students access the College Application Manager, they will be prompted to complete a three-part setup process. Follow the steps below to get set up!
Click College in the side navigation bar, then select College Application Manager.
Click Let's go on the Welcome to College Applications window
 
Personal Details
Add the required Personal Details
*Note: this information is required for certain documents requested by colleges and can be edited at any time.
 
Fee Waiver Eligibility
Indicate Fee Waiver Eligibility
*Note: if marked as eligible, a required Fee Waiver document will be added for the counselor to complete. Eligibility can be edited at any time.
 
FERPA Waiver
FERPA gives you the right to review confidential letters of recommendation under certain circumstances if one of the following conditions is met:
You are enrolled in college, and that college saves the recommendations for enrolled students
You are 18 or older.
Waiving your right lets colleges know that you do not intend to read your recommendations, which helps reassure colleges that the letters are candid and truthful.
Important Note: Common App requires its own FERPA waiver to be signed
Complete & electronically sign the FERPA Waiver, then click Finish application setup.
*Note: you can lick “Sign Waiver” again to change your FERPA Waiver decision as long as no documents have been submitted for any of your applications. See more below.
Edit College Application Setup
Click the pencil icon to edit your personal details or fee waiver eligibility.
Click Review to edit your FERPA waiver. The FERPA Review pop-up module will display the date you last updated your FERPA waiver and allow you to change your selection. Update your selection and click Sign Waiver again.
* Note : Your FERPA waiver cannot be changed once documents have been submitted for any of your applications.

title: Add College Application - North Creek High School
content:
Add College Application
Adding college applications into SchooLinks ensures that all documents required by colleges are requested from your counselor, such as transcripts and counselor recommendations. Additionally, once added to your College Application Manager, you will be able to organize and manage your own checklist items as well as request teacher recommendation letters for each application.
This will walk you through the steps on how to add:
Non-Common App applications
Common App Applications
Add an Application
Click College in the side navigation bar, then select College Application Manager.
*Note: if this is your first time accessing the College Application Manager, you will need to first complete the 3-part setup process. Learn more at  College Application Manager Overview & Setup
 
Click Add Application from List in the top left corner to start tracking an application for a college on your Final List.
This section provides an overview of how many applications you have added, categorized by the four Final List categories: Guaranteed, Likely, Target, and Reach schools, helping you track progress and maintain a balanced application strategy.
*Note: Learn how to build a final list at  How to Build a Final List
 
Alternatively, you can click Add Application in the top right-hand corner and use the search bar to add an application for a college that you did not add to your Final List.
 
Application Status: select the application status for this application: in-progress, completed & pending, etc, then click Add Application.
 
Application Method: select the method through which you will be submitting this application. Every application method accepted by the college will be listed here. Follow the appropriate section below depending on the application method selected.
Non-Common App Application Method
6. Application Type: select the application type for which you are applying: early decision, regular decision, etc...
7. Application Deadline: provide the date the application is due.
*Note: some application deadlines are auto-fulfilled if already verified by SchooLinks. For unverified deadlines, find the application deadline on the college's website.
8. Doc Destination: if the college is in-network with Parchment , this field will display the following message:
Doc Destination: "This college is In-Network. We'll make sure your materials are sent electronically where they need to go"
If the Doc Destination field is empty, you will be prompted to enter either an email or a mailing address. This address is where materials submitted by your counselor and teachers will be submitted.
9. Program Name (Optional): Only fill in this field if you're applying to a program that requires a different application.
10. Student Requirements: select any financial aid and/or scores & performance items that apply for this application. Any items selected will be added to your student checklist for this application. *Note: if a school requires test scores or a self-reported academic record to be submitted, then those items will be auto-selected for you.
11. Click Save Application when all required details have been added
Common App Application Method
If applying to schools via Common App, be sure to link your Common App account in SchooLinks first. Learn more at  Connect Common App Account .
6. After selecting the Common App method, click Add to My Colleges, then Add College to Common App
7. Once you are redirected to the Common App website, log in to Common App with your Common App credentials (these may be different than your SchooLink login credentials)
8. Once logged in, a pop-up window will appear confirming that the selected college has been added to your Common App My Colleges list. Click Okay .
9. Add your Preferred Start Term and Preferred Admission Plan under the General tab of the college name on the Common App Dashboard. This will provide your counselor with the application type and deadline in SchooLinks.
10. Return to the SchooLinks tab and click Refresh Page to sync the application details in SchooLinks.
*Note: to refresh Common App data manually at any time, click the Click here to manually refresh! button within the Common App section of the College Application Manager SchooLinks side panel.
Application Requirements

content:
Options for High School & Beyond
This page is a fantastic place to learn about - or more about - those in-district and out-of-district options available to students struggling with high school completion.
IMPORTANT NOTE:   The out of district options have external links.  These websites are not controlled or operated by the Northshore School District.
Graduation Alliance works together with Northshore School District to provide a research-based approach to alternative education. Holistic in nature, pairing time and place flexibility with the social-emotional supports that many at-risk and non-traditional students require in order to stay on track for graduation, and successfully transition to life after high school.
Lean more HERE
Students who attend Northshore Networks experience a high-level of teachers support and learning focused on student readiness, talent, interest, and personal responsibility. 
Learn more HERE
Grades 11 and 12 only for the 2024-2025 school year. 
The Northshore Online Academt is a program for families who choose to learn in an online learning format for students that is coordinated and taught by Northshore School District teachers and in conjunction with Edgenuity (secondary only).
Learn more HERE
Innovation Lab High School (ILHS) is a choice school within the Northshore School District and currently serves just under 250 students, grades 9-12. The facility is a non-traditional learning space designed to be highly flexible and configurable. ILHS is a member of the first cohort in the Washington State Board of Education's Mastery Based Learning Collective (MBLC) and is also a leader in the State of the implementation of mastery-based learning. mStudents are held to rigorous standards-base expectations and participated in project-based learning at the classroom level. personal passion projects, and school-wide interdisciplinary projects. 
Learn more HERE  
Secondary Academy for Success (SAS) serves grades 9-12, embracing students whose learning styles require different instructional approaches who need or want an alternative setting to the large comprehensive high schools. 
Learn more HERE
The Alternative Learning Experience (ALE) is public education, available to all public school districts and public charter schools in Washington state, where some or all of the instuction is delivered outside of a regular classroom schedule. The intent of ALE is to ensure that studetns have educational opportunities designed to meet their individualized needs. ALE fallows all public education requirements as well as WAC 392-550 .
Graduation Alliance works together with Northshore School District to provide a research-based approach at alternative education. Holistic in nature, Pairing time and place flexibility with the social-emotional supports that many at-risk and non-traditional students require in order to stay on track for graduation, and successfully transition to life after high school. 
Learn more HERE
Market Square Alternative Learning Experience (ALE) is public education where the instruction is delivered online. Market SQuare's ALE Follows all public Education requirements and the public school year. 
Learn more HERE
Students who attend Northshore Networks experience a high-level of teachers support and learning focused on student readiness, talent, interest, and personal responsibility.
Grades 11 and 12 only for the 2024-2025 school year. 
Learn more HERE
The Northshore Online Academy is a program for families who choose to learn in an online environment. This program provides an online learning format for students that is coordinated and taught by Northshore School District teachers and in conjunction with Edgenuity (secondary only).
Learn more HERE
 
Washington Virtual Academies (WAVA), a program of Omak SChool District, is a fuul-time online public school for students in grades K-12. We're dedicated to inspiring and empowering student through an education experience tailored to each child's needs.
Learn more HERE.
Insight School of Washington (ISWA) is a full-time online public school for K-12 students. WE're dedicated to inspiring and empowering students through an education experience tailored to each child's needs.
Learn more HERE
High School+ (HS+) is a competency-based high school diploma program for adultt learners, 18 years and older, who do not have a high school diploma or equivalency (GED).
High School+ programs turn life experiences, work experiences, previous high school credit, and any military experience into credits towards a high school diploma.
To learn more about HS+, eligibility requirements, and the benefits of a HS+ program, click HERE
To begin identifying a program that fits your needs, click on the program of interest below. 
The HS+ program offers a Washington State high school diploma for those 18 years and older. Students can apply previously earned high school credits, job trainings, or life experience with our curriculum to finish their coursework. Students must be 18 years of age or older at the time of enrollment. Students can fit HS+ around their schedule as classes are online.
Learn more HERE
The high school+ program is an ability based program that takes into account your life experiences and your previous high school credits and guides you towards earning your high school diploma! This amazing program takes your skills and knowledge through a prior learning class and helps you find ways to show how you've met some of the minimum requirements for your high school diploma. This is a great program for anyone who is turning 18 or older and looking to earn their diploma!
Learn more HERE
The High School+ program at Lake Washington Institute of Technology consists of adult basic education classes for students looking to improve their skills or pursuing an adult high school completion diploma. The program includes building of basic skills- reading and writing - along with courses in science, history, and literature. Our goal is to prepare HS+ students for college classes.
Learn more HERE
Get credit for what you already know! If you've earned some high school credits, have work or life experience, but no high school diploma or equivalent, High School+ may be the prefect fit for you.
Learn more HERE
Open Doors (WAC 392-700) is a free statewide youth re-engagement system designed to help at-risk students work toward earning their WED, high school diploma, a two-year college degree, and/or a technical or vocational certificate. Many Open Doors programs are dual-credit (where students earn both high school and college credit simultaneously) and create non-traditional pathways for high school students, age 16-21, to earn a high school diploma and more.
To learn more about Open Doors, eligibility requirements, and the benefits of an Open Doors program, click HERE
To begin identifying a program that fits your needs, click on the program of interest below.

Holistic in nature, pairing time and place flexibility with the social-emotional supports that many at-risk and non-traditional students require in order to stay on track for graduation, and successfully transition to life after high school.
Learn more HERE
Open Doors re-engages disconnected youth through programs that create multiple pathways for students and provides avenues to life after high school. Coursees can be done anywhere, anytime. Most of them will be online. Start anytime - even mid-year. Students can even attend throughout the summer to complete their learning journey.
Learn more HERE
The program enables students to learn academic English and work toward an AA degree, GED, high school diploma or professional/technical certificate while receiving wrap-around services and support in order to achieve their educational goals. Learn more out LIP via the Info Session Presentation .
Learn more HERE
Part of the Open Doors program through Lake Washington Technical Academy (LWTA), the Language Intensive Program (LIP) is designed to provide linguistic, academic, and cultural knowledge, and wrap-around support to English language learners.
Learn more HERE
The Career Education Options (CEO) program enables youth to work toward their high school diploma, GED, or other professional-technical and AA-degree credential while receiving wrap-around services and support to help them succeed in their educational pursuits.
Learn more HERE
EvCC offers Youth Re-Engagement (U3) in partnership with local school districts and Sea Mar Community Health Centers. U3 is designed to meet students' specific and individual needs and goals. Instead of starting with the Foundations quarter, some students may start with other classes, including ESL, Basic Skill Building, High School Completion, technical/vocational, or college-level classes. One of our main goals in making the U3 Program work for you.
Learn more HERE

title: Link - North Creek High School
content:
Link
What is a Link Leader?
A Jaguar Link Leader is an individual who represents North Creek High School – connecting incoming Freshman to our community, and helping them to do their best here in their new school. To be a North Creek High School Jaguar Link Leader you need to be committed, respectful, enthusiastic, self-confident, self-directed, positive, accountable, willing to lead others, willing to take risks, and have strong communication skills. If you do your job well, the students you mentor will become integral parts of a positive climate and culture at North Creek, and will commit themselves to doing their best academically throughout their four years here.
Expectations of a LINK Leader
Attend all the mandated training days
Check in and connect with 9th graders regularly throughout the school year (text, email, invite them to and attend socials together, check in to see how they're doing, etc.)
Lead activities during advisories and planned Link activities
Serve as a positive role model for the 9th grades
Mandatory Dates for Link Leader Training
If you would like to become a Link leader, there are dates that have  mandatory attendance as these are required dates for leadership training.  If you are not available for all of the required dates, please do not apply .  If you are chosen to be a leader and fail to show up for training for any reason, we will need to remove you from your Link leader position.
ALL DATES SUBJECT TO CHANGE PENDING SCHOOL SCHEDULE
Every Link Leader is REQUIRED to attend the following dates without exception:
Development Day
May 27th, 2026  2:00 p.m. - 4:00 p.m.
Training 1
August 20, 2026  9:00 a.m. - 2:00 p.m.
Training 2

Check-In
August 28, 2026  9:00 a.m. - 11:00 a.m.

Sept 1, 2026, 6:45 a.m. - 3:45 p.m.
Link Leader Application 2026-2027
The Application for 2026-2027 Link Leaders is  OPEN HERE . The deadline to apply is  March 30th, 2026 .
Frequently Asked Questions
 
WOULD I BE A GOOD LINK LEADER?
We are looking for KIND, DEPENDABLE, and POSITIVE students who can think on their feet and have a genuine interest for making NCHS as great as it can be.
HOW DO I APPLY?
The Application for 2026-2027 Link Leaders will be posted in March, along with the deadline, which is typically mid- to late-March.
HOW WILL LINK LEADERS BE CHOSEN?
Applications will be evaluated based on a standard rubric as well as using teacher recommendations. We are looking for a diverse group of leaders who have a variety of interests and come from different backgrounds. Our Link Leaders should represent the entire student body. Most importantly, Link Leaders should treat others with kindness and compassion and can be counted on to meet their commitments.
HOW COMPETITIVE IS THE PROGRAM?
There are limited spots based upon the number of the incoming Freshman class. If you aren't accepted into the program this year, we strongly encourage you to join the A-team and also apply again next year.

These low cost plans are used by many school districts across the state. Although they are not the only provider of this type of coverage, they have been recommended by our Washington Schools Risk Management Pool.
2026-27 SPORTS PARTICIPATION FEE INFORMATION
All students participating in a sport at the high school level (including Competitive Cheer)  must purchase a high school $70 ASB card  (ILHS card is $45). These funds go directly into the school’s ASB account to support the year-to-year cost of the athletic programs. Costs such as facilities, equipment, uniforms, game transportation cost, etc.

The fee will start at $775 per athlete and may be adjusted depending on participation numbers. Should expenses surpass the $775 initial fee, an additional fee assessment will be required for each athlete. Any surplus funds will be refunded to participating families.
The fee does not guarantee a spot on the athletic team, playing time, or a letter award, and it does not waive the requirement for participating students to purchase an ASB card. This fee, due prior to the first interscholastic competition, will be paid at the school. Students from low-income families may qualify for a fee waiver. Students who need assistance should contact their school counselor, administrator, coach, or athletic director for information.

title: Injuries at School and Optional Insurance - Northshore School District
content:
Injuries at School and Optional Insurance
The health and safety of our students is of critical importance to the Northshore School District.  Even so, accidents may happen sometimes resulting in costly medical bills. Please note that the district does not carry insurance for student personal injury costs and therefore cannot assume responsibility for them. This includes students participating in athletics.
If your student is injured during school activities you, as the guardian, are responsible for any medical bills.
When a student is injured or ill at school, or during any school sponsored event:
A staff member will provide immediate care to the student unless or until the staff member is relieved by a nurse, doctor or emergency personnel.
The parent/guardian will be contacted except in the case of very minor injuries that, in the judgement of the school nurse or staff person, do not pose a serious risk to the student.
In the case of a medical emergency 911 will be called.
Transport to nearest hospital may be necessary.
Parents/Guardians please note:  It's important keep your emergency contact information up-to-date with your child's school.

All communications and updates will be done through Final Forms and will only be received by those who have registered.
Here is the link to register: https://northcreek.nsd.org/athletics/register-for-athletics  
ELIGIBILITY:
You must be registered in Final Forms and be eligible (i.e., not red) to participate in summer open gyms and tryouts. Please take care of this early. There are no eligibility exceptions. If your status is yellow or grey, you can participate in tryouts and training, but you must be green before you can play in a match.
SPRING ACTIVITIES:
No need to register
WEIGHTS AND CONDITIONING
Wednesday / Friday,  March 11th - June 17th
6:30 a.m. - 7:40 a.m.
Weights and Conditioning will be held in the Weight Room in Building 3 at North Creek High School.
Building 3 doors facing the student parking lot open at 6:30 a.m.
Wear comfortable, athletic clothing and bring water. No need to bring volleyball-specific gear like kneepads.
We will finish by 7:40 a.m. and open the locker room to give you ample time to get dressed and ready for school.
This activity is only open to current NCHS students.
OPEN GYMS
Tuesday / Thursday - June 4th - June 18th
4:00 p.m. - 6:00 p.m.
Open gyms will be held in the Main Gym in Building 3 at North Creek High School
Wear comfortable, athletic clothing and bring water. Bring any volleyball-specific gear you like to wear, like kneepads and ankle braces.
Current 8th graders (incoming 9th graders) are highly encouraged to attend.
SUMMER ACTIVITIES:
Must register in Final Forms for Summer Volleyball and be eligible (i.e., not red)
OPEN GYMS
Tuesday / Thursday, June 23rd - July 30th
4:00 p.m. - 6:00 p.m.
Open gyms will be held in the main gym at North Creek High School
Wear comfortable, athletic clothing and bring water. Bring any volleyball-specific gear, like knee pads and ankle braces, that you like to wear.
Current 8th graders (incoming 9th graders) are highly encouraged to attend.
TEAM CAMP
July 8 - July 11 at Washington State University in Pullman, WA
We will leave from the North Creek High School student parking lot on July 8th. 
We will return to the North Creek High School parking lot on July 11th. 
Registration is directly with WSU with this link: https://wsuwomensvolleyballcamps.totalcamps.com/shop/product/560927 *select the "PAY ONLINE - Team Overnight" when you register.   Note: this is an external link and not operated by Northshore School District.
Registration will be limited to 18 athletes, as we only have transportation for 18 to Pullman.
A field trip form is required for attendance. This will be emailed out to those who register.
More information about what to pack, when to meet, and what to expect at camp will be sent via email to those who register.
JUNIOR JAG CAMP
We will be hosting a Junior Jag Camp in the NCHS Gym from Tuesday, July 28th, to Thursday, July 30th.
Camp for incoming 3rd through 5th-grade campers will be held from 9:00 a.m. to Noon, and camp for incoming 6th through 8th graders will be from 1:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m.
Camp will include learning all volleyball skills and positions, and will conclude with a tournament on the final day of camp. No prior experience necessary.
All campers will receive a Jaguar Volleyball Camp T-Shirt
Additional information about what to expect at camp and what to bring each day can be found at the registration link below.
Registration is available at this link: https://wa-northshore-lite.intouchreceipting.com/NCHSVolleyballYouthCamp  
PRE-TRYOUT BOOSTER CLINIC
Boosters plan to host a pre-tryout clinic the week before tryouts for all prospective players who are interested, led by a local, high-level volleyball coach.
Registration information will be updated here when available.
TRYOUTS 
You must be registered in Final Forms for Fall Volleyball and be eligible (i.e., not red) to try out. No exceptions . Tryouts will be held in the NCHS Main Gym starting Monday, August 24th, and teams will be selected by the end of practice on Wednesday, August 26th.
Monday, August 24th - Sign in and warm up from 3:30 p.m. - 4:00 p.m. - please arrive by 3:30 p.m. to ensure we are able to check everyone in on time. Evaluations will begin at 4:00 p.m. and end at 6:30 p.m.
Tuesday, August 25th - Gym will open at 3:30 p.m. to warm up. Evaluations will go from 4:00 p.m. to 6:30 p.m. The first cut will happen at the end of this practice.
Wednesday, August 26th - Gym will open at 3:30 p.m. to warm up. Evaluations will go from 4:00 p.m. to 6:30 p/m. The teams will be selected, and the final cut will happen by the end of this practice.
PRACTICES AND GAME DAY SCHEDULES
Practice days and times will be on non-game days throughout the school week from 3:45 p.m. - 6:00 p.m. for all three teams unless otherwise communicated by the coach. 
Games this season are scheduled to be on Mondays and Wednesdays
C and JV Games begin at 5:15 p.m.
Varsity Games begin at 7:00 p.m.
The game schedule can be found on Arbiterlive - be sure to use the drop-down to select the 26-27 season, as it defaults to showing 25-26 currently.
Tournaments: Each team will participate in at least 2 tournaments this season. These tournaments are subject to change, but this is the schedule with the most current information available.
C - Saturday, Sept 12 @ Jackson High School and Saturday, Sept 26 @ Monroe
JV - Sat, Sept 17 @ Jackson High School + TBD

North Creek Golf
The Jaguar golf program prides itself on being a place where athletes can be part of a team that is supportive, inclusive, challenging, and most of all, a lot of fun! Golf is a sport that has at its cornerstones honor, integrity, sportsmanship and dedication. During our practices we focus on the fundamentals of the full swing, chipping and putting, as well as the mental part of the game, including course management, strategy, and maintaining a positive outlook and demeanor (golf can be frustrating!). We typically have eight or nine matches a year in the KingCo Conference, the most competitive golf conference in Washington. Our athletes are fortunate to have the opportunity to play some of the best courses in the region, including Sahalee, Inglewood, Bear Creek, The Plateau Club and Snoqualmie Ridge.
To try out to be a varsity golfer, you should be able to shoot under 100 for 18 holes. To be a JV golfer, you should have some golf experience and be able to get around the course under 120 strokes. All golfers should have an understanding of the basic rules of golf. Our hope always is that our golfers enjoy the Jaguar golf experience enough that they return throughout their high school years and leave as confident and capable players! We stress that golf is a lifetime sport - one that you can enjoy with people of all ages and backgrounds and continue to play well into your senior years.

If we do not have a third coach, we will cut to around 50 or the average for the other teams in our district.  It is critical that we have high numbers in FinalForms to prove to the district we need a third coach. 
Practice will be M-F up until our last match in October.  We will have practice the first Saturday, Aug. 29 and Saturday and/or Monday of Labor Day Weekend.  Our first match is scheduled for Sept. 10th. 
The KingCo ADs have reorganized the 4A teams again.  Our Crown Division now includes North Creek, Bothell, Woodinville, Juanita, Lake WA, and Redmond.
